stories.headline: US and Canada Trade Tensions Escalate as Canada Vows Retaliatory Tariffs
stories.body:
Trade relations between the United States and Canada have worsened after bilateral negotiations broke down late on Friday. In response, the US imposed new 50% tariffs on a wide range of Canadian products. The US duties took effect at 12:01 am on Saturday and cover approximately $20bn worth of Canadian imports. This amount represents roughly 5% of Canada's total exports to the US. American President Donald Trump announced the levies to counter what he described as Canadian discrimination against American automobiles, dairy products, and alcohol. Last year, total trade in goods and services between the two neighbours reached $880bn, while the broader USMCA agreement underpins $1.6tn in annual trade among the US, Canada, and Mexico.

The newly targeted Canadian products include wine, dairy, cement, clothing, and hockey equipment. Several Canadian whisky brands, including Crown Royal, Canadian Club, and Black Velvet, could also be affected. These new measures build upon existing US tariffs that already apply to Canadian steel, aluminium, automobiles, and lumber. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated on Fox & Friends Weekend that the US had been prepared to reduce tariffs on steel, autos, and lumber under a proposed deal. However, Greer accused Canada of causing the collapse of talks by refusing to finalise an agreement despite receiving favourable terms. Greer later added on Fox News that there are no current plans to resume negotiations.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he suspended negotiations and ordered Canada's negotiating team to return to Ottawa following last-minute changes to the US proposal. Carney called the new US tariffs a "miscalculation" designed to "hurt and divide us". He announced that Canada will respond with matching "dollar-for-dollar" retaliatory tariffs starting 8 September. Canada's planned tariffs will apply to American steel, dairy, home appliances, and electronics. Last year, several Canadian provinces had already removed US-made alcoholic drinks from retail shelves after President Trump introduced an initial round of duties.

Canadian political leaders across the country expressed strong support for the retaliatory stance. Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed Carney's actions and stated that President Trump "can't be trusted". British Columbia Premier David Eby warned that accepting American trade restrictions would reduce Canada "to the economic equivalent of the 51st state".

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Strikes as Escalation Warnings Grow
stories.body:
Cross-border attacks between Russia and Ukraine have intensified alongside stern warnings from Moscow. Russian President Vladimir Putin stated in an interview that Ukraine opened "Pandora's box" by striking Russia's economy. He threatened to attack Ukraine's most vulnerable economic sectors in response and rejected current peace proposals as "strange" and "unacceptable". Overnight, Ukrainian drones struck an industrial facility and an Ozon logistics centre in Chapayevsk. Ozon is Russia's second-largest online retailer. Russia's Defence Ministry reported shooting down 457 Ukrainian drones overnight. Meanwhile, Ukrainian strikes killed two children in a Krasnodar port town and killed two people while injuring 13 in the Belgorod region.

Russian attacks also caused significant casualties in Ukraine. The death toll from a Friday double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rose to 16, with 130 people injured. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called the attack "terror by design" and called for new sanctions. A day earlier, Russian strikes on Kyiv killed 17 people, and a strike in Mykolaiv killed four people, including three children. Ukraine's defence ministry previously noted its ballistic missile interception rate is roughly 40%. Amid the violence, leaders from France, Germany, and the UK plan to co-chair a support meeting in Kyiv on Monday.

stories.headline: US Criticizes Israeli Strikes in Syria for Lack of Prior Warning
stories.body:
A series of military actions by Israel in Syria has drawn criticism from Washington. US Special Envoy for Syria Tom Barrack criticized an Israeli strike on a disused military air base at Abu Duhur as an "unnecessary escalation" and stated that Israel gave no prior warning before the attack. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz countered that Israel had provided intelligence to authorized US parties prior to the strike. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Turkey was attempting to establish a military presence at the base. However, Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani stated Turkish personnel visited only for ongoing training cooperation. Amid the dispute, Turkey announced it is seeking an Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over genocide allegations.

In separate actions, an Israeli drone strike hit a delivery truck near Beit Jinn in southwestern Syria, injuring a civilian driver. The Israeli military stated it targeted a terrorist planning immediate attacks, while Qatar condemned the strike as a violation of Syrian sovereignty. This follows a late November Israeli ground raid in Beit Jinn that left 13 civilians dead and six Israeli soldiers injured. Syria's interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa reaffirmed that his government does not seek conflict with Israel.

stories.headline: US Federal Judge Blocks Trump Administration Visa Ban Covering 75 Nations
stories.body:
A US federal judge has blocked a key immigration initiative enacted by the Trump administration. US District Judge Jeannette Vargas struck down a policy that suspended immigrant visa processing for citizens from 75 nations. Judge Vargas, who was appointed to the judiciary by former President Joe Biden, ruled that Secretary of State Marco Rubio exceeded his statutory authority in issuing the suspension. The policy, implemented in January, affected nationals from countries including Afghanistan, Brazil, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Somalia, Thailand, and Yemen.

The legal challenge was brought by 11 individual plaintiffs and two non-profit organisations, including CLINIC. In defending the ban, the State Department cited data showing that over 30 percent of households with immigrants from the targeted 75 countries received public assistance. This court decision follows a separate ruling in June where another federal judge overturned administrative restrictions on asylum, work permits, green cards, and citizenship applications. The US government retains the right to appeal Judge Vargas's decision to a higher court.

stories.headline: PM Modi Addresses New BJP Leadership Team as Party Passes Vande Mataram Resolution
stories.body:
The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) held its first official meeting with its newly constituted national leadership team on August 22, 2026, under party president Nitin Nabin. Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the newly appointed office-bearers and urged them to intensify their outreach efforts toward young people. Following this guidance, party president Nitin Nabin instructed the leadership team to focus on "Yuva Samvad" dialogue initiatives aimed specifically at individuals aged 14 and above. As part of these broader public outreach efforts, the BJP announced a month-long nationwide campaign named 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan', scheduled to run from September 17 to October 17.

The newly named national leadership team under Nitin Nabin comprises 65 members, including 51 new faces. The leadership lineup includes 12 women and six representatives from minority communities. Key organizational appointments include Vasundhara Raje Scindia and Ram Madhav as national vice presidents, while Smriti Irani was named one of the party's eight national general secretaries. Additionally, Piyush Goyal was reappointed to serve as the BJP's national treasurer.

During the meeting, the party passed a 10-point resolution condemning a recent decision by the Congress Working Committee. The resolution criticized the Congress party's choice to restrict the singing of Vande Mataram to only its first two stanzas. In response to criticisms, Congress MP KC Venugopal stated that his party remains firmly committed to its historic 1937 decision on Vande Mataram, which was originally established by Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The political debate follows national legislative action taken earlier in 2026, when Parliament enacted the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act to grant Vande Mataram statutory legal protection equal to that of the National Anthem.

stories.headline: Cargo Ship Sinks Off Odisha Coast Prompting Maritime Rescue Operation
stories.body:
A major maritime rescue operation is underway in the Bay of Bengal after a foreign cargo vessel sank on August 22, 2026. The Panama-flagged vessel, named MV Oceanwinner, went down roughly 240 nautical miles off the coast of Paradip in Odisha. The ship had departed Paradip port at 10:30 p.m. on August 20 carrying 1,700 tonnes of iron ore fines bound for China, though initial reports also stated the cargo was bound for Singapore.

There were 24 crew members aboard the vessel when it sank. The crew consists of 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals, and one Bangladeshi national. The Indian Coast Guard and the Indian Navy immediately launched search and rescue operations. According to Coast Guard DIG Sanjay Negi, the search operations are being directed by the unit stationed in Andaman and Nicobar. A senior IPS officer informed PTI that rescue teams have successfully pulled two crew members out of the water alive. Search efforts continue for the remaining crew members.
